passages.text: This mind is always anxious, this mind is always stressed about stresses that haven’t arisen and those that have. If there is a state free of anxiety, please answer my question. Not without understanding and fervor, not without restraining the sense faculties, not without letting go of everything, do I see safety for living creatures.
passages.note: Constant anxiety and worry; seeking peace of mind

passages.text: “Do you delight, ascetic?” “What have I gained, sir?” “Well then, ascetic, do you sorrow?” “What have I lost, sir?” “Well then, ascetic, do you neither delight nor sorrow?” “Yes, sir.”

Fools and simpletons behave like their own worst enemies, doing wicked deeds that ripen as bitter fruit. It’s not good to do a deed that plagues you later on, for which you weep and wail, as its effect stays with you. It is good to do a deed that doesn’t plague you later on, that gladdens and cheers, as its effect stays with you.
passages.note: Being your own worst enemy; regret and choices

passages.text: Suppose a cart driver leaves the highway, so even and well compacted. They enter upon a rough road, and fret as soon as their axle is broken. So too, a dullard leaves the good to follow what’s against the good. Fallen in the jaws of death, they fret like one whose axle is broken.
passages.note: Straying from the good path and its consequences
